model: Sum-of-parts: owner FCF DCF of the recurrent businesses plus Rail plus Property pipeline, associates and hybrid capital in the equity bridge (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Interests in associates and joint ventures at book
equity_bridge.note: Interim 2026 balance sheet (30-Jun-2026). Share of profit HK$787m FY2025 (after HK$380m Hangzhou Line 1 impairment), HK$771m H1-2026; ~10% return on book, so book is a fair, not generous, proxy. Their profit is excluded from the engine flows (recurrent EBITDA is pre-associates).

equity_bridge.item: Existing-site HK property development pipeline, PV of post-tax profit net of remaining property payments
equity_bridge.note: Sites on already-built lines plus Oyster Bay (LOHAS Pkg 13, THE SOUTHSIDE Pkg 6, Ho Man Tin and Tai Wai sell-through, Yau Tong, Pak Shing Kok, Tung Chung Traction Substation, Kam Sheung Road Ph2 share, Oyster Bay 860,500 sqm). Schedule (HK$bn post-tax): H2-2026 3.0, 2027 7, 2028 6, 2029 6, 2030 5, 2031 6, 2032 4, 2033 4, 2034 3, 2035 3, 2036-40 1.5/yr (~HK$55bn undiscounted, vs HK$54bn booked 2019-2025); less ~HK$8.8bn of remaining 2026-28 property payments (HK$10.3bn guided 2026-28 less HK$1.5bn paid H1-2026). Discounted at 7%. Excludes the new-line sites (TCE, A16, Kwu Tung, Hung Shui Kiu, Northern Link), which are in the R+P programme item.

equity_bridge.item: Recovery of property development in progress (HK$43,378m book), at a 50% timing/risk haircut
equity_bridge.note: PDIP (interim note 16) is land premium, site formation and development cost already sunk; booked profit is struck AFTER transferring PDIP out, so future cash receipts = profit + PDIP recovered. PDIP has been sticky (41.7bn FY2023 -> 43.4bn H1-2026; only HK$897m transferred out in FY2025), so recovery is long-dated: valued at ~50% of book.

equity_bridge.item: New-line R+P programme NPV (HK$140bn capex 2026-2034 vs funding-gap land grants and new-line operating cash)
equity_bridge.note: Project agreements size the land-premium reduction to bridge each line's funding gap at a commercial return (interim note 22(iii)); South Island Line (HK$17bn capex, ~HK$25bn+ of THE SOUTHSIDE profit roughly a decade later) is consistent with an IRR only modestly above WACC. Valued at ~7% of the ~HK$110bn PV of programme capex. This item, not the engine, carries the new lines' capex, revenue and site profit.

equity_bridge.item: Investments in securities outside MTR's net-debt definition
equity_bridge.note: Investments in securities HK$17,973m less HK$16,700m of bank MTNs/bonds/CDs already netted in net debt (interim p.27-28).

equity_bridge.item: Perpetual capital securities (US$3bn, June 2025) at face
equity_bridge.note: Classified as equity under IFRS but senior to ordinary shareholders; ~5.3% distribution (HK$618m H1-2026). Excluded from shareholders' equity in core_metrics; in kpis as PerpetualCapitalSecurities.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 1.7% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 5.5% and EPS 3yr CAGR 14.1%. Revenue CAGRs run off the COVID trough (FY2020 42,541 -> FY2025 55,465) and are flattered by overseas concessions now lost; EPS growth is property-development timing (FY2023 dev profit HK$2.1bn vs HK$11.1bn FY2025). Book equity barely grows because dividends (~HK$8.2bn/yr) absorb most underlying profit.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs undefined: owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC; interest income not stripped because MTR is in net debt) was negative every year FY2020-FY2025 (FY2021 -396, FY2022 -4,169, FY2023 -1,498, FY2024 -1,062, FY2025 -7,852). EPS 5yr CAGR undefined (FY2020 loss). SBC is immaterial (~0.24% of revenue) so the reported vs owner FCF gap is not an SBC story; it is capex > depreciation plus property receipts classified in investing.

scenario_narratives.base: The core HK rail network earns little cash while fares are frozen and the HK$65bn renewal programme runs, then recovers to a ~7-8% owner-FCF margin by the early 2030s as the Fare Adjustment Mechanism resumes; the value rests on that recovery, the malls and station retail inside the same flows, and a property pipeline worth roughly HK$61bn (existing sites + PDIP recovery + modest new-line NPV) that is mostly already committed.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fare catch-up after 2027/28, tourist-driven station retail and faster capex normalisation take recurrent margin back to the pre-COVID 38.5% and owner-FCF margin above 10%; the property and new-line items are held at base in the bridge, so the bull case here is a recurrent-business bull only (a stronger HK residential market would add roughly HK$2-4/share via the pipeline).
scenario_narratives.bear: The majority owner keeps fares capped as costs rise, renewal capex never normalises, and Mainland/overseas operations keep shrinking; recurrent owner FCF stays thin through the decade. A HK residential downturn would additionally cut the existing pipeline (not modelled per scenario: roughly HK$2-3/share for a 30% cut).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sum of parts on a cash basis. The market capitalises MTR's underlying profit (~HK$16bn/yr, two-thirds property development) as if it were a perpetual distributable stream; this model does not, for two reasons visible in the filings. First, recurrent accounting profit overstates recurrent cash because existing-network maintenance/renewal capex (~HK$14bn/yr guided 2026-28) is more than double depreciation (HK$6.4bn) while fares are frozen - consolidated FCF has been negative six years running and the ~HK$8.2bn/yr dividend plus HK$1.2bn of perpetual distributions are being funded by debt and property receipts. Second, under R+P the new-line property profit is the land-premium reduction that bridges each line's funding gap, so it is a capital grant matched against HK$140bn of new-line capex, not free earnings; the matched pair is valued at a modest positive NPV. Only the already-granted pipeline on built lines is valued as profit.
key_risks_to_valuation: Fare Adjustment Mechanism: frozen 2025/26 and 2026/27; whether the deferred increments are ever released is the single largest driver of the recurrent value and is a policy decision of the majority owner.
HK residential cycle: the existing-site pipeline (HK$31.5bn) and PDIP recovery (HK$21.7bn) are held at base in all scenarios; a 30% cut moves value by ~HK$2-3/share.

R+P new-line NPV is a judgment (HK$8bn): if land grants prove generous (Southside-style surpluses) the programme could be worth several times that; if construction overruns on six to seven concurrent projects, it is negative.
Maintenance capex: the long-run 18% of revenue assumption is ~1.3x depreciation; each 1pp of revenue in terminal capex is worth ~HK$1.2/share.

Market-implied view differs sharply: the price implies capitalising property development profit as a perpetuity; consensus targets (~HK$32-33) use SOTP with HK rail at regulated asset value and investment property at fair value.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 26.16-37.88
data_sources.financials: 0066.HK_Metrics.csv and kpis (core_metrics, HKD millions); FY2025 Annual Report consolidated cash flow (lines 12480-12510), segment table (lines 13780-13800), PDIP note 24 (line 15542); Interim Report 2026 business review and financial position (lines 1640-1930), PDIP note 16, related-party note 22 on R+P land premium (line 4300), property packages tables (lines 1180-1215).
data_sources.qualitative: 0066.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10): fare freezes, HK$140bn new-line pipeline, HK$65bn renewal, UK/Stockholm exits, Hangzhou impairment, Sydney Metro West.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated cash flow, 'Share-based payments' add-back HK$132m (0066.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:14040); no net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0). ShareAwardSettlement (HK$113m) is the cash purchase of shares that funds the award scheme, i.e. the same cost, not added again.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E run-rate (base_revenue = 2 x H1-2026 revenue HK$26,231m plus normal H2 seasonality; UK Elizabeth Line/SWR exited May-2025 and Stockholm Metro Nov-2025 are already out of the H1-2026 base). Year 1 of the projection is FY2027.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:05Z regular close (HKEX Friday close; Yahoo chart API)
inputs.share_count_basis: 6,224.82m shares in issue at 30-Jun-2026; FY2025 diluted weighted average 6,224.97m (AR FY2025 line 14676). Held FLAT: SBC (~0.24% of revenue) is expensed in the flows, there are no buybacks, and scrip issuance has been negligible since FY2021.
inputs.net_debt_basis: MTR's own net-debt definition at 30-Jun-2026 (interim p.27-28): loans and other obligations HK$170,355m + obligations under service concession HK$9,839m = HK$180,194m, less cash, bank balances and deposits HK$113,997m and bank MTNs/bonds/CDs HK$16,700m = HK$130,697m. Ties to the reported 21.7% net debt-to-equity x total equity HK$228,458m = HK$49,575m. Gross cash is high because H1-2026 pre-funded the new-line programme with HK$58bn of AUD/HKD/EUR green bonds.
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD-built (HKD is USD-pegged): risk-free 3.6% (HK 10y Exchange Fund Note ~ US 10y less peg spread), ERP 5.5%, beta 0.65 (regulated monopoly, ~75% HKSAR Government-owned, fare formula) -> cost of equity ~7.2%; borrowings at 3.5% weighted average cost (interim 2026) -> 2.9% after 16.5% HK tax; perpetual capital securities ~5.3% (HK$618m per half on HK$23.5bn). Weights ~73% equity / 18% debt / 9% hybrid -> 6.3%, rounded to 6.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged in the flows (fare mechanism, capex, property cycle), not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt. IFRS-16 lease liabilities (HK$1,346m at FY2025) sit inside 'loans and other obligations' in net debt; lease principal (~HK$255m/yr) is not deducted from flows. The KCRC Rail Merger service-concession FIXED annual payment (HK$750m/yr) is likewise held as the HK$9,839m concession obligation in net debt and NOT charged in the flows. The VARIABLE annual payment to KCRC (HK$3,330m FY2025, ~6.0% of revenue, tiered on KCR-system revenue) is a genuine operating charge and is carried in lease_cost_pct_path. MTR's reported EBITDA is stated BEFORE the VAP, so leaving it out would overstate cash flow by ~HK$3.3bn/yr.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of subsidiaries); the NCI stock (HK$688m at 30-Jun-2026, mostly Chinese Mainland subsidiaries) is deducted once in the equity bridge. Immaterial either way.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. MTR straddles two rows of the routing table, so it is valued as a sum of parts (SKILL.md: 'value the parts separately and sum'). (1) The RECURRENT businesses - HK transport operations, station commercial (retail/advertising), HK property rental and management, and the Chinese Mainland and international rail/property subsidiaries - are an operating company and go through the owner-FCF component engine. MTR's 'total revenue' already excludes property development profit, so the engine revenue base is recurrent only, and recurrent EBITDA (HK$17,701m FY2025; HK$8,954m H1-2026) is pre-VAP, pre-associates. (2) PROPERTY DEVELOPMENT is lumpy, cyclical, inventory-type profit tied to land grants and is NOT capitalised as a growing perpetuity inside the engine (that would read HK$12.2bn of H1-2026 profit as run-rate). It enters the equity bridge as an explicit PV of the pipeline. (3) NEW RAILWAY LINES (HK$140bn programme through 2034) are R+P projects: under the project agreements the land premium on the line's sites is 'full market value less the agreed reduction amount for bridging the funding gap' (interim note 22(iii)), i.e. the property grant is sized to give MTR a commercial return on the line. The new-line capex, the new lines' fare income and the property profit on their sites are therefore valued together as ONE bridge item at a modest positive NPV; their capex is excluded from the engine capex path and their revenue from the engine growth path, so nothing is counted twice. (4) Associates/JVs (Beijing, Shenzhen, Hangzhou metros, Octopus) are not in recurrent EBITDA and enter the bridge at book. (5) The US$3bn perpetual capital securities rank ahead of ordinary equity and are deducted at face. WHY NOT reported FCF: consolidated FCF is negative FY2020-FY2025 (-7,720 FY2025) because property receipts sit in investing and new-line capex sits in capex; last_fcf = reported_fcf - SBC per the house formula is recorded for audit but the engine builds from components. Recurrent-only FY2025 cash: OCF 11,874 - fixed+variable annual payments 3,775 - recurrent capex 11,403 (HK transport assets 10,115 + investment property 341 + Shenzhen Line 13 833 + other 114) - SBC 132 = about -3.4bn, and OCF there still carries ~HK$2bn of property-development tax. The core issue the model surfaces: maintenance/renewal capex (HK$41.9bn guided for 2026-28, ~HK$14bn/yr) is more than twice depreciation (HK$6.4bn) while fares are frozen, so recurrent accounting profit materially overstates recurrent cash. SBC is ~0.24% of revenue (near SBC-zero market); kept explicit. No buybacks: the flat count is a modelling convention the company does not fund, but dilution is negligible. Balance sheet is 30-Jun-2026 while year 1 is FY2027: H2-2026 recurrent FCF (~-HK$0.8bn) is omitted and H2-2026 property profit is in the pipeline bridge item.

bear.narrative: The fare formula stays politically capped (affordability cap tied to flat median household income, further freezes or social concessions imposed by the majority owner) while maintenance, wage and energy costs rise 4%/yr, so HK transport EBIT stays negative; Hangzhou Line 1 and other Mainland JVs keep underperforming and more overseas concessions are lost on re-tender. Renewal capex overruns and stays above 20% of revenue in perpetuity.

base.lease_cost_note: Variable annual payment to KCRC, FY2025 HK$3,330m = 6.0% of revenue; tiered on KCR-system revenue (top tier 35%), so it rises as a share when HK fare revenue grows faster than the overseas book.
base.capex_note: Existing-network maintenance/renewal only (HK$41.9bn guided 2026-28 = ~HK$14bn/yr, plus ~HK$0.5bn/yr Mainland/overseas and investment-property fit-out). New-line capex is in the R+P bridge item. Long-run 18% of revenue is ~1.3x depreciation, a normal replacement-cost premium for a 40-year-old network.
base.cash_tax_note: HK profits tax 16.5%, but the Board of Review ruled fixed and variable annual payments non-deductible (2011/12-2017/18, under appeal), and Mainland/Australian operations tax at 25-30%; FY2025 recurrent tax ~17% of pre-tax, 20% on post-VAP EBIT charges the VAP non-deductibility.
base.narrative: Fares stay frozen through 2026/27 and the Fare Adjustment Mechanism resumes ~2.5%/yr increases from 2027/28 once the affordability cap rolls off; HK patronage +1-2% on cross-boundary/HSR strength; station commercial and malls grow with inflation; the Mainland/international book (~HK$17.5bn revenue at ~7% EBITDA margin) is roughly flat as Sydney Metro West does not start until 2032. Recurrent EBITDA margin drifts up from 33.8% to 35.5% on mix. The HK$65bn renewal programme keeps capex above 20% of revenue until ~2031 before normalising at 18%.

bull.narrative: Deferred FAM increments are released once the household-income affordability cap expires after 2027/28 (fare catch-up of 3-4%/yr for two years), cross-boundary and HSR patronage keep compounding with Northern Metropolis integration, and station retail recovers toward pre-2019 margins on tourist flows. Capex normalises faster as the signalling and train-replacement programmes finish. Margin reaches 38.5%, the pre-COVID recurrent level.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default because fares are set by a formula the ~75% government owner has frozen two years running and the recurrent business is a single-regulator dependency. Base 50% as the FAM mechanically resumes once the affordability cap cycle ends. Bull cut to 25% from 35% because it needs both a fare catch-up and an early capex normalisation, two independent things going right.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is ~0.24% of revenue (near SBC-zero market): house and street differ by ~HK$0.6/share, so the band collapses and a band position is meaningless (the formula divides by ~0.6 and returns thousands of percent). Reported as null.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
